title: No signal at the bus stop
setting: A Saturday afternoon in the countryside. Yuki and Kenta have just hiked down a mountain to a small bus stop at the bottom, and they want to know when the next bus back to town comes.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: haa, yatto basutei made kita. tsugi no basu, nanji kana?
lines.ja: はあ、やっとバス停まで来た。次のバス、何時かな？
lines.kana: はあ、やっとばすていまできた。つぎのばす、なんじかな？
lines.english: Phew, we made it to the bus stop at last. What time's the next bus, I wonder?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: chotto matte. netto de shirabete miru.
lines.ja: ちょっと待って。ネットで調べてみる。
lines.kana: ちょっとまって。ねっとでしらべてみる。
lines.english: Hang on, I'll look it up online.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: ありがとう。スマホ、充電切れちゃってさ。
lines.kana: ありがとう。すまほ、じゅうでんきれちゃってさ。
lines.english: Thanks. My phone's battery died, see.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: are? nanka netto tsunagaranai n da kedo.
lines.ja: あれ？なんかネットつながらないんだけど。
lines.kana: あれ？なんかねっとつながらないんだけど。
lines.english: Huh? The internet's not working for some reason.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yama no naka da kara ne. koko, denpa warui n ja nai?
lines.ja: 山の中だからね。ここ、電波悪いんじゃない？
lines.kana: やまのなかだからね。ここ、でんぱわるいんじゃない？
lines.english: Well, we're out in the mountains. The signal's probably bad here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto da. denpa warukute, nanimo mirenai.
lines.ja: ほんとだ。電波悪くて、何も見れない。
lines.kana: ほんとだ。でんぱわるくて、なにもみれない。
lines.english: You're right. The signal's so bad I can't load anything.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa, basu no jikan ga wakaru apuri toka, irete nai no?
lines.ja: じゃあ、バスの時間がわかるアプリとか、入れてないの？
lines.kana: じゃあ、ばすのじかんがわかるあぷりとか、いれてないの？
lines.english: Then haven't you got an app or something that tells you the bus times?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: irete nai. sore ni, apuri mo netto tsunagaranai to tsukaenai yo.
lines.ja: 入れてない。それに、アプリもネットつながらないと使えないよ。
lines.kana: いれてない。それに、あぷりもねっとつながらないとつかえないよ。
lines.english: Nope. Besides, apps don't work either if the internet's down.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sokka. jaa, ikkai dengen kitte, mata irete mitara?
lines.ja: そっか。じゃあ、一回電源切って、また入れてみたら？
lines.kana: そっか。じゃあ、いっかいでんげんきって、またいれてみたら？
lines.english: Oh, right. Then why not try switching it off and on again?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: dame. dengen irete mo, yappari denpa warui.
lines.ja: だめ。電源入れても、やっぱり電波悪い。
lines.kana: だめ。でんげんいれても、やっぱりでんぱわるい。
lines.english: No good. Even after turning it back on, the signal's still bad.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: matte. mou ikkai netto de shirabete miru kara.
lines.ja: 待って。もう一回ネットで調べてみるから。
lines.kana: まって。もういっかいねっとでしらべてみるから。
lines.english: Wait. I'm going to try looking it up online one more time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: iya, netto de shirabenakute mo ii kamo. hora, ushiro.
lines.ja: いや、ネットで調べなくてもいいかも。ほら、後ろ。
lines.kana: いや、ねっとでしらべなくてもいいかも。ほら、うしろ。
lines.english: No, I don't think you need to look it up online. Look, behind you.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e? a, jikokuhyou! zutto koko ni atta n da.
lines.ja: え？あ、時刻表！ずっとここにあったんだ。
lines.kana: え？あ、じこくひょう！ずっとここにあったんだ。
lines.english: Huh? Oh, the timetable! It was right here the whole time.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: tsugi wa sanji yonjuppun da tte. ato juppun da yo.
lines.ja: 次は3時40分だって。あと10分だよ。
lines.kana: つぎはさんじよんじゅっぷんだって。あとじゅっぷんだよ。
lines.english: The next one's at 3:40, it says. That's ten minutes from now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: よかった。でも一応、アプリ入れとく。
lines.kana: よかった。でもいちおう、あぷりいれとく。
lines.english: Phew. I'll still get the app, though, just in case.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: ネットがつながったらね。
lines.kana: ねっとがつながったらね。
lines.english: Once the internet's working, that is.

questions.english: What happens at the bus stop?

choices.english: Yuki's phone works again after she switches it off and on, so she finds the bus time online.
Kenta's phone has died, so they miss the bus and have to wait another hour.
They can't get online to check the bus times, then Kenta spots the timetable right there at the stop.

questions.explanation: In line 2 Yuki offers to look up the next bus online (netto de shirabete miru). In line 4 the internet won't connect (netto tsunagaranai), and in lines 5-6 they put it down to the bad signal in the mountains (denpa warui). In lines 9-10 switching the phone off and on doesn't help. In line 13 Kenta says she doesn't need to look it up online and points behind her, and in line 14 Yuki sees that the timetable was there all along. A is wrong: in line 10 the signal is still bad after she turns the phone back on, and they get the time from the timetable, not the internet. B is wrong: Kenta's phone has died (line 3), but they don't miss the bus. The next one comes in ten minutes (line 15).

questions.english: You and Kenta want to see a film tonight. He asks, "nee, kono eiga, nanji kara da kke?" You don't know. Offer to look it up online.
questions.ja: ねえ、この映画、何時からだっけ？
questions.kana: ねえ、このえいが、なんじからだっけ？
questions.romaji: nee, kono eiga, nanji kara da kke?
questions.answer: Say you'll look it up online: netto de shirabete miru (let me look it up online), or netto de shiraberu ne. Keep de, because the internet is the tool you look things up with.

modelAnswers.romaji: wakannai. chotto netto de shirabete miru.
modelAnswers.ja: わかんない。ちょっとネットで調べてみる。
modelAnswers.english: No idea. Let me look it up online.

modelAnswers.romaji: nanji da kke. chotto matte, netto de shiraberu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 何時だっけ。ちょっと待って、ネットで調べるね。
modelAnswers.english: What time was it again? Hang on, I'll look it up online.

questions.explanation: When Kenta wonders about the bus, Yuki says 'chotto matte. netto de shirabete miru' (line 2) and says it again in line 12. In line 13 Kenta tells her 'netto de shirabenakute mo ii kamo' (no need to look it up online). de marks the internet as the means, the same way as sumaho de or jisho de. The thing you check takes o (eiga no jikan o netto de shiraberu). shiraberu is for checking facts like times and meanings. For finding a place such as a shop, use sagasu (netto de sagasu). Kenta asks casually, so answer casually. Adding -te miru makes it a friendly offer.

questions.english: When Yuki tries to look up the bus on her phone, something goes wrong. What does she say?
questions.ja: スマホを見て、ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: すまほをみて、ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sumaho o mite, yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: The internet won't connect for some reason.
choices.romaji: nanka netto tsunagaranai n da kedo

choices.english: The internet isn't working (hataraku: work, as a person does a job).
choices.romaji: nanka netto hatarakanai n da kedo

choices.english: The internet won't move (ugoku, as for a frozen app).
choices.romaji: nanka netto ugokanai n da kedo

questions.explanation: In line 4 Yuki says 'are? nanka netto tsunagaranai n da kedo.' When Wi-Fi or mobile data fails, Japanese says the internet doesn't connect (tsunagaranai). Yuki says it again in line 8 (netto tsunagaranai to tsukaenai), and Kenta uses it in line 17 (netto ga tsunagattara ne). B is wrong: hataraku is 'work' in the sense of a person doing a job, so this copies English 'isn't working' word for word. C is wrong: ugokanai (won't move) is for a frozen app or device, not for a connection that won't come up.

questions.english: You're out in the countryside when Kenta calls. The line keeps breaking up, and he says, "moshimoshi? kikoeru? nanka, yoku kikoenai n da kedo." Tell him it's the signal.
questions.ja: もしもし？聞こえる？なんか、よく聞こえないんだけど。
questions.kana: もしもし？きこえる？なんか、よくきこえないんだけど。
questions.romaji: moshimoshi? kikoeru? nanka, yoku kikoenai n da kedo.
questions.answer: Apologise and blame the signal with denpa ga warui. In casual speech ga drops: gomen, koko denpa warui n da. To give the bad signal as the reason for something, use the -kute form: denpa warukute.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, koko denpa warui n da. ato de mata kakeru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、ここ電波悪いんだ。後でまたかけるね。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, the signal's bad here. I'll call you back later.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, denpa warukute, kotchi mo yoku kikoenai.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、電波悪くて、こっちもよく聞こえない。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, the signal's bad. I can't hear you well either.

questions.explanation: Kenta says 'koko, denpa warui n ja nai?' in line 5. Yuki says 'denpa warukute, nanimo mirenai' in line 6 and 'yappari denpa warui' in line 10. Phone signal is denpa ('radio waves'). Don't say shingou, which means a traffic light, or the loanword shigunaru. warui covers both broken-up calls and pages that won't load. If there's no signal at all, say denpa hairanai. Kenta is a friend, so drop ga and answer casually.

questions.english: Once they've found the timetable, Yuki says, "demo ichiou, apuri iretoku." What is she going to do?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、何をしますか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なにをしますか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: Turn her phone back on and try the internet again.
Get the bus-times app on her phone anyway, just in case.
Put her phone away in her bag, since they don't need it now.

questions.explanation: Line 16: apuri iretoku is apuri o ireru (get an app, literally 'put it in') plus -toku (do it ahead of time). It's the kind of app Kenta asked about in line 7 (basu no jikan ga wakaru apuri toka, irete nai no?), and in line 8 she said she didn't have it (irete nai). That's why Kenta jokes in line 17 that she'll have to wait until the internet works. A is wrong: turning the phone on is dengen o ireru, which she already tried in line 10, and here the thing she 'puts in' is the app, not the power. C is wrong: ireru can mean putting something into a bag, but she said apuri, and nobody mentions a bag. Note that English 'get the app' is not apuri o morau, which would sound as if someone handed it to you.
